newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar surges as funds dump U.S. dollars.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar surges as funds dump U.S. dollars.

text.p: The Singapore dollar shot up in late afternoon trade on Thursday on stop-loss sales by funds that were long the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
"Some stops were triggered below 1.4350. They could be very huge, especially by U.S. funds, which have been very long the U.S. dollar," a European bank dealer said.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4295/305 to the U.S. unit at 0710 GMT against a morning low of 1.4367.
U.S. funds had been building long dollar/Sing positions since last week as anxieties about regional currencies spread following the Thai central bank's shock move to a managed float of the baht.
"I think it's a healthy correction. I would buy the (dollar/Sing on) dips to see it back above 1.44," the dealer said, adding that dollar/Sing should remain supported around 1.4290/1.4300.
She said the Singapore dollar had been pushed up alongside a sharp rise in the ringgit as Malaysian interbank rates surged due to expectations of a liquidity squeeze.

"Dollar/Sing has followed dollar/ringgit for the past few days. I think the Sing is being dragged by the ringgit move," she said, adding that the ringgit was pushed up by a sudden rise in the Kuala Lumpur overnight interbank rate.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.4900/05 to the dollar at 0910 GMT after firming to 2.4875 against 2.5005/10 in the morning.

The overnight rate rose to a high of 45/50 percent on sudden tightening of liquidity in the banking system as a result of Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday to support the ringgit.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers said it could mop up anything between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit from the system.
Settlement of Tuesday's intervention is on Thursday.
